comment: Senate Class II seats (last elected 2020), plus OH and FL special elections. dem_seats_not_up / rep_seats_not_up reflect current composition minus seats being contested.

races.note: Tommy Tuberville running for governor instead. Open R primary: Steve Marshall (AG), Barry Moore (Rep), Jared Hudson among leading candidates. Deep-red state remains Safe R.

Mary Peltola (former congresswoman, lost House seat 2024) challenging Sullivan. Ranked-choice voting. 6 named-candidate polls: recent 4 (Jan '26–Oct '25) avg D+1.6; summer '25 polls showed R+1 to R+4. Race has trended toward Peltola. Alaska has a history of electing crossover candidates.
Cotton seeking third term in deep-red Arkansas. Democrat Hallie Shoffner, a farmer and first-time candidate, won the D primary. Cotton's 33.6-pt 2020 margin and R+24 PVI make this Safe R.

Hickenlooper seeking re-election (says this will be his final Senate term). Faces a D primary challenge from state Sen. Julie Gonzales. No major R challenger has emerged. Colorado has shifted solidly blue at the federal level. Safe D.
Coons running for a fourth term in deep-blue Delaware. R primary features only minor candidates. No Republican has won a Senate race in Delaware since 1994. Safe D.

Special election for Marco Rubio's vacated seat (Rubio became Secretary of State). Ashley Moody (R, former FL AG) appointed. D primary: Vindman, Nixon, Jenkins, Mujica. 8 polls avg R+7.0. Emerson (Mar '26): Vindman R+8, Nixon R+11, Mujica R+7. MDW (Apr '26, unrated): Vindman R+1 — outlier vs field. PPP (Apr '26, D-sponsored): Vindman R+3.

Won by 1.2% in January 2021 runoff; top Republican target in 2026. R primary: Carter, Collins, Dooley, King. 18 polls (Jan '25–Mar '26) across 8 pollsters avg D+5.3 vs likely nominees. Ossoff leads all R candidates except Kemp (unlikely to run). Most recent Emerson (Mar '26): D+3 to D+8 depending on R opponent.
Risch (age 83 at election) confirmed running for re-election with Trump's endorsement. Faces minor R primary challengers and a weak D field. Deep-red Idaho (R+32) keeps this Safe R.

Dick Durbin retiring. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the D primary (March 17) with 40% over Krishnamoorthi and Kelly. Former IL GOP chair Don Tracy won the R primary. Stratton is heavily favored in deep-blue Illinois.

Joni Ernst retiring. R primary June 2: Hinson vs Carlin (Hinson heavily favored). D primary June 2: Wahls vs Turek (both strong fundraisers). Change Research (Jan '26) shows Hinson +3 vs all D candidates. PPP (Aug '25, D-sponsored) showed Ernst era tighter at R+1 to D+2. Iowa has trended solidly R.
Marshall seeking re-election with only minor R primary opposition. A crowded D primary (8 candidates) will select a nominee Aug 4, but deep-red Kansas (R+20) keeps this Safe R.

Mitch McConnell retiring after 42 years. R primary: Rep. Andy Barr, former AG Daniel Cameron, Nate Morris. D candidate: Charles Booker. PPP polls (D-sponsored, Dec '25) show Morris only +1 vs Booker, Cameron +7, Barr +11. Avg vs named R candidates: R+6.3. If Morris wins the R primary, this could be more competitive than PVI suggests — but R+26 keeps it Safe R.

Cassidy faces a serious R primary challenge from Rep. Julia Letlow, who has Trump's endorsement, due to Cassidy's vote to convict Trump in his second impeachment trial. Former Rep. John Fleming also running. D field is weak. Louisiana remains Safe R regardless of primary outcome.

Collins is a moderate R who historically outperforms PVI by 10+ pts. D primary: Platner avg D+4.0 across 11 polls (range: tied to D+11); Mills avg R+0.3 (much weaker). MPRC (Mar '26, n=1167): Platner +9 — latest and strongest Platner result. If Platner wins primary, this is a genuine toss-up trending D; if Mills, Collins likely holds.

Markey (age 80) seeking a third full term. Rep. Seth Moulton is mounting a significant D primary challenge on generational change. Polls show Markey leading Moulton by 13-23 pts. No credible R challenger in D+30 Massachusetts. Safe D.

Gary Peters retiring. D primary ongoing: McMorrow, Stevens, El-Sayed. R candidate Mike Rogers. 21 polls (Mar '25–Jan '26) across 7 pollsters avg R+2.5. Stevens polls best (avg R+0.5), McMorrow middle (avg R+2.9), El-Sayed weakest (avg R+6.0). Rosetta Stone (Oct '25) outlier polls (R+7, R+7, R+14) pull avg rightward. Race tightened in Jan '26 Emerson polls.

Tina Smith retiring. D primary (Aug 2026): Flanagan leads Craig by 3–30 pts in early polls. R candidate: Michele Tafoya. Emerson (Feb '26) shows both Flanagan and Craig at ~D+6.5 vs Tafoya. PPP (Sep '25) showed D+2 to D+4 vs generic R. Minnesota leans D.
Hyde-Smith won the R primary (March 10) with 81%. She faces Democrat Scott Colom, Lowndes County DA. No Democrat has won a MS Senate race since 1982. Safe R.

Steve Daines withdrew minutes before filing deadline and endorsed Kurt Alme (U.S. attorney). Controversial last-minute maneuver designed to clear the R primary field. Open seat adds uncertainty but Montana remains solidly R.

Dan Osborn (Independent) challenging Ricketts, who was appointed in 2023 after Ben Sasse resigned. Osborn nearly beat Deb Fischer in 2024 and is a strong populist candidate. Polls show Ricketts +1. Osborn would likely caucus with Democrats for Senate control. Modeled on D side for control purposes.

Jeanne Shaheen retiring. Pappas (D) vs Sununu (R) is the competitive matchup: 9 polls avg D+3.6 (range D+2 to D+7). Emerson Mar '26 shows D+2 — tightest Sununu matchup yet. Pappas dominates Brown matchup at D+10 avg. If Sununu wins R primary, this is a top-tier battleground; if Brown, likely D hold.
Booker seeking a third full term. R primary features only minor candidates. NJ has not elected a Republican senator since 1972. Safe D.
Only GOP candidate (Christopher Vanden Heuvel) disqualified for insufficient petition signatures. No Republican will appear on the general election ballot — first time in modern NM history.

Thom Tillis not seeking re-election; open seat. Roy Cooper (former governor) is a strong D recruit. R primary held March 3 — Whatley is the nominee. Cooper leads Whatley in 11 of 11 included polls (avg D+5.8, range D+0 to D+10). Quantus (Apr '26, n=987): D+5. TIPP outlier (D+24) excluded. Top Democratic pickup opportunity.

Markwayne Mullin confirmed as DHS Secretary, resigned March 23. Gov. Stitt appointed Alan Armstrong (Williams Companies exec) on March 24; Armstrong signed an oath not to run for the full term. R primary June 16: Rep. Kevin Hern is the frontrunner (Bice opted for House re-election). D primary: Evan Beck, Jim Priest among declared candidates. Deep-red state remains Safe R.
Merkley seeking a fourth term. Oregon has not elected a Republican senator since 2002. Safe D.
Reed seeking re-election to a sixth term. RI has not elected a Republican senator since 2000. Safe D.

Graham only +2 vs generic D and +6 vs Andrews in D-sponsored PPP polls (Nov '25). Avg R+4. Graham is personally unpopular but R+11 PVI keeps this Safe R. Worth monitoring if a strong D candidate emerges.
Rounds seeking a third term. Faces only minor R primary opposition. Won by 31 pts in 2020; deep-red South Dakota (R+27) keeps this Safe R.
Hagerty seeking a second term with Trump's endorsement and nearly $9M raised. No R primary challenger. Deep-red Tennessee (R+26) keeps this Safe R.

R primary headed to runoff (Paxton vs Cornyn). 14 Talarico polls (Sep '25–Mar '26) across 7 pollsters avg R+1.4. Range: D+2 (PPP, Impact Research) to R+6 (Ragnar, UT Tyler). Impact Research Mar '26 shows Talarico +1/+2 vs Cornyn/Paxton. Talarico polls better vs Paxton than vs Cornyn. Bruising R primary could depress general election turnout.
Warner seeking a fourth term. The most notable R challenger, state Sen. Bryce Reeves, withdrew in December 2025. Remaining R field lacks a top-tier recruit. Likely D.
Capito seeking a third term with Trump's endorsement. R primary challenge from convicted Jan. 6 participant Derrick Evans poses no real threat. Deep-red WV (R+30) keeps this Safe R.

Cynthia Lummis announced in December 2025 she will not seek re-election. Rep. Harriet Hageman, endorsed by Lummis, is the frontrunner in the R primary (Aug 18). Deep-red Wyoming (R+35) remains Safe R regardless.

Vacancy election for J.D. Vance's Class III seat, on the November 2026 midterm ballot alongside all other races. Gov. DeWine appointed Jon Husted (former Lt. Gov.) in Jan 2025. Sherrod Brown (lost his OH Class I seat in 2024) running to return to the Senate. Race tightened from Husted +6 (early 2025) to near-even through early 2026 (EMC Feb '26 Brown +4, OnMessage Mar '26 Brown +2), but April polls show Husted reasserting a lead (Echelon R+6, BGSU R+3). 12 polls avg R+2.2.
